title: OnPrem-VPC bundle strategy labnotes
body:
Purpose
---
Working experiment notes for a compact set of bundle configs and sensitivity checks to present to pricing and SRE for Private deployments (on-prem vs VPC). These are intentionally lightweight: assume we'll convert the promising configs into an interactive sheet later. This doc is a ledger of experiments, heuristics, and ops concerns — not the final proposal.

Context & scope
---
- Audience: product, pricing, solutions-eng, SRE.
- Scope: small-to-medium enterprise customers evaluating on-prem appliance vs VPC private tenant. Focus on licensing + support mix, three-year TCO, and breakpoints for recommended bundles.
- Goal: surface simple bundle templates that map to three buyer archetypes (startup, mid-market, enterprise) and show sensitivity to utilization and GPU pricing.

Assumptions (baseline)
---
- Workload: 1.2B tokens/day (avg) -> ~438M tokens/year.
- Model: open LLM variant, serving profile equivalent to ~45% of Llama3-XXL baseline for latency/cost.
- On-prem HW: 8xA100-80GB equivalent per cluster for baseline; capex per GPU = $30k, rack+network+ops contribution = $120k; useful life 3 years (straight-line depreciation).
- VPC: monthly instance equivalent cost = $12k/month for reserved pool (committed).
- License fee (platform): baseline list = $200k/year for private control plane (on top of infra).
- Support tiers (annual): Standard = 15% of license, Premium = 25% of license + 2 FTEs of onboarding retainer for enterprise.
- Ops labor: internal ops 0.25 FTE per cluster for startups, 1.0 FTE for enterprise deployments (salary loaded = $220k/year).
- Network egress/other: negligible for private; include 5% overhead for monitoring, backups.

Quick TCO model (3-year, rounded) - baseline numbers
---
Inline calc notes: keep numbers intentionally coarse to find breakpoints. Unit notation: $k = thousand.

On-prem (baseline cluster):
- HW (8 GPUs): 8 * $30k = $240k
- Rack + infra = $120k
- Total capex = $360k -> depreciated over 3y = $120k/year
- License = $200k/year
- Support (Standard 15%) = $30k/year
- Ops labor (0.25 FTE) = $55k/year (0.25 * 220k)
- Maintenance spares / power / network = $40k/year
- Yearly total (on-prem) = $120k + $200k + $30k + $55k + $40k = $445k/year
- 3-year total = $1.335M (excludes end-of-life replacement)

VPC private tenant (baseline):
- Reserved infra commit = $12k/month -> $144k/year
- License = $200k/year (same control plane pricing assumption)
- Support (Standard 15%) = $30k/year
- Ops labor (0.1 FTE, vendor-managed) = $22k/year
- Network/monitoring overhead = $20k/year
- Yearly total (VPC) = $144k + $200k + $30k + $22k + $20k = $416k/year
- 3-year total = $1.248M

Observation: base-case gap relatively small (~$87k over 3 years) — suggests buyers will choose based on non-cost factors (compliance, control, latency). Focus bundles on where cost matters: scale, utilization, and support intensity.

Sensitivity experiments (high level)
---
1) Utilization swing (+/- 40% tokens)
- On-prem: fixed capex means per-token cost falls with utilization. If tokens +40% -> per-year effective cost stays same -> unit cost down 29%.
- VPC: if we can autoscale down in VPC, commit vs on-demand mix matters. For low-utilization customers (<60% of reserved), VPC becomes attractive.

2) GPU price decline (Capex reduction by 25%)
- On-prem 3y becomes $360k * 0.75 = $270k -> yearly depreciation $90k -> annual on-prem = $415k -> gap closes/reverses toward on-prem.

3) Support sensitivity (enterprise premium)
- Premium support + onboarding adds $70k/year + 2 FTE retainer ($150k) -> +$220k/year. For enterprise buyers, license/support dominates, both on-prem and VPC move similarly.

Bundle experiments (three starter bundles)
---
1) Essentials (startup-friendly)
- Target: small teams, proof-of-concept, <0.5B tokens/day.
- Offer: 1-year on-prem starter appliance option or VPC trial with pay-as-you-go and optional 6-month reserved commit at 50% discount.
- Pricing: License = $75k/year, Support Standard = 12% (intro), Onboarding workshop (one-time) = $15k.
- Ops: included basic onboarding + runbook.
- Why: reduce entry barrier.

2) Growth (mid-market)
- Target: steady production usage 0.5–2B tokens/day.
- Offer: Dedicated private tenant (VPC) with reserved capacity + optional on-prem cluster with financing option. License = $150k/year. Support = 18%. 1-year commit with optional 2-year amortized HW financing.
- Add-on: Model tuning seat + performance review (one-time $30k).

3) Enterprise (regulated, SLA-critical)
- Target: >2B tokens/day, strict compliance.
- Offer: on-prem or VPC private control plane but with enterprise SLA, premium support (25%+), dedicated CSM + 2 FTEs for onboarding/ops. License = $350k/year. Support = 25%+ retainer.
- Add-ons: Quarterly on-site/remote performance review and a guaranteed fallback capacity in hosted fleet for blitz traffic.

Breakpoints & recommendation heuristics
---
- If customer expects >70% utilization of an on-prem cluster across 3 years -> recommend on-prem appliance (capex amortized wins).
- If customer values quick start and expects high variance in daily tokens (spiky) -> recommend VPC with burstable reserved + on-demand overlay.
- If support intensity is primary concern (multi-region compliance, guaranteed RTO) -> enterprise bundle with premium support and white-glove ops (both deployment models offered).

Operational notes & risks
---
- HW delivery lead times: 3–6 months for high-end GPUs. For sales, this means financing + temporary VPC overlay options should be in bundles.
- Warranty and spare parts: include 10% spares budget and 1 extra GPU slot for hot swap in on-prem pricing.
- Security controls: customers often require KMS/HSM integration. This should be a priced optional add-on with a one-time integration fee ($25k–$75k depending on scope).
- Model licensing risk: if customer wants OEM/closed weights, add separate model licensing pass-through.

Open questions / TODOs
---
- Run param sweep sheet: varying tokens/year (100M -> 2B), GPUs (4,8,16), support tiers, and GPU capex reductions (0%, 25%, 40%). Create an interactive sheet for sales by 2024-10-10.
- Confirm whether license baseline should scale with qps or tokens; currently we assume flat license but some customers want usage indexing.
- Validate ops FTE assumptions with SRE (Priya to own).
- Draft short sales play: financing + VPC overlay for hardware lead time gap (Liam to draft).

Quick wins to include in next PRD
---
- Standardize three bundles above in a modular quote template.
- Add an explicit line item for temporary VPC overlay to cover HW lead times (monthly priced).
- Add optional KMS integration and white-glove onboarding retainer as allowed add-ons in price config.

Appendix: compact sensitivity matrix (annualized numbers, $k/year)
---
Notes: baseline numbers from main section. Columns: tokens low/ baseline/ high. Rows: on-prem yearly / vpc yearly / delta (onprem - vpc).

Tokens: 250M | 438M (baseline) | 700M
On-prem yearly: 375 | 445 | 445 (capex fixed so small change in ops)
VPC yearly: 210 | 416 | 620 (VPC scales with commit changes and on-demand)
Delta (onprem - vpc): +165 | +29 | -175

Interpretation: at small scale VPC cheaper (no capex), at baseline parity, at high scale on-prem cheaper because VPC on-demand/reserved costs grow with committed capacity.

End notes
---
Keep these as labnotes. Once we pick 1–2 promising bundle templates we'll build the canonical pricing sheet and a short executive memo summarizing recommended default.

Last edits: 2024-10-03 by Maya Chen (draft for pricing review).
